findings.title: New fixture docstring cites internal RULE./SCAN. ids meaningless to a REPL reader
locations: fixture/GBG Fixture/src/FixtureC.jl:41-49 (new `span` function and its docstring)
findings.before: (no such function or docstring existed at base; FixtureC.jl had no `span` binding)
findings.after:
"""
    span(options) -> (lo, hi)

The iteration bounds of an [`Options`](@ref) record; internal, so it needs no page home. The argument
`options` is the record. Returns the pair.

Two arguments and a returned tuple: RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM binds fewer than three in running prose, and
SCAN.ARGS_FORM must read the parameter list as the parenthesis that closes the first one — a parser
that stopped at the last `)` counted the return tuple as three more parameters and demanded bullets.
"""
span(options::Options) = (1, options.iterations)
findings.why_it_matters: A reader who runs `?span` (or opens this docstring on any page it is ever homed to) hits two bare identifiers — `RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM` and `SCAN.ARGS_FORM` — that resolve to nothing outside `policy/RULES.toml` and `catalog/scans.toml`; the paragraph is also architectural rationale about a bug in the SCANNER's own parenthesis-matching, which RULE.DOC.HOME_ORDER's own exclusion list ("implementation internals ... architectural rationale") explicitly keeps out of a function docstring. This is the one instance of this pattern anywhere in the fixture — every other fixture docstring reads as clean, self-contained prose — so it is a new precedent, not a continuation of an existing one, and it evades the existing SCAN.DEAD_REF pattern (which only matches `§`, `docs/`, `ALLCAPS.md`, `inspiration/`) even though it is exactly the class of thing RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS and RULE.DOC.SELF_CONTAINED are written to prevent.
findings.description: The diff adds a new `span(options)` fixture function whose docstring, after the ordinary identity/argument/returns prose, appends an explanatory paragraph about why the SCAN.ARGS_FORM parenthesis-matching bug in GBGCodingTools' own scanner used to mis-parse this exact signature. That explanation is meta-commentary for a future maintainer reading the source, not documentation of what `span` does — but it lives inside the rendered docstring body, so it is exactly as reachable to a REPL reader as the rest of the text, in a package whose own rubric (RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS, RULE.DOC.SELF_CONTAINED, RULE.DOC.HOME_ORDER's exclusion list) exists specifically to keep this kind of content out.
